basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et peregrinatus est in Geraris. Nam et verbo peregrinationis et nomine Gerarae, id est'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et peregrinatus est in Geraris. Nam et verbo peregrinationis et nomine Gerarae, id est incolatus, decenter sanctorum vita figuratur, quae, quantum divinis mancipata praeceptis, tantum a temporalibus est alienata gaudiis; unde et Apostolus eorumdem patriarcharum vitam glorificans aiebat: Fide moratus est Abraham in terra repromissionis, tanquam in aliena, in casulis habitando cum Isaac et Jacob cohaeredibus promissionis ejusdem; exspectabat enim fundamenta habentem civitatem, cujus artifex et conditor Deus (Heb. XI, 9). Et paulo post: Juxta fidem defuncti sunt omnes isti, non acceptis repromissionibus, sed a longe eas aspicientes et salutantes, et confitentes quia peregrini et hospites sunt super terram (Ibid., 13). Qui enim haec dicunt significant se patriam inquirere; erat autem Geraris olim terminus Chananaeorum ad meridiem, et civitas metropolis Palaestinae, posita inter Cades et Sur, hoc est inter duas solitudines, quarum una Aegypto jungitur, ad quam populus transfretum Rubri maris pervenit, altera vero Cades usque ad Sarracenorum eremum extenditur.
